notes: Tapping the record player no longer lifts the whole app. The jump scrolled its row into view with scrollIntoView, which on Android bubbles straight out of the list container and scrolls the page itself — so the header and the nav pills rode up with it. It now animates the list’s own scroll position, which is the only thing that moves

And it goes to the album rather than the playlists view. The tap target inside the turntable still carried the older listener, which switched the active playlist to All Songs and re-navigated after the album had already been opened — so tapping the record player while a playlist was on screen landed you back in playlists. The turntable tap now handles the jump on its own

The track list header (playlist or album name, track count, total time) is a contained card now instead of a full-bleed bar. Its edge-to-edge background and bottom rule cut across the theme, which is what made it look like it was protruding past the rest of the UI on every theme; it uses the raised theme surface, rounded corners and the same side insets as everything else

Get song opens the actual Spotify app. Spotify’s site is allow-listed for the converter, and that is exactly what kept the link inside SideCut: allow-listed hosts load in the app’s own WebView, so it put a logged-out Spotify web player on screen. The tap now uses the spotify: scheme, which Android hands to the installed Spotify app — and if there is no Spotify app, the full track link is copied for the converter instead of opening the embedded player

Mark all as read lives in the New releases panel, not on the Home bubble. The floating check chip on the bubble card is gone; the panel has a proper filled button with a check icon and the live count (“Mark all 12 as read”), which reads “All caught up” once there is nothing left
